text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.6% today as oil prices and refiner sentiment deteriorated on mixed geopolitical signals. The stock lost $33 in three trading days after hitting $424.89 on September 18th—a sharp reversal driven by headlines suggesting potential U.S.-Iran diplomatic progress, which eased immediate concerns about supply disruptions and oil prices. Crude fell back below $110 per barrel (U.S. benchmark), undercutting the higher margins refiners had enjoyed when tensions were spiking.

The uncertainty itself is also weighing on the sector. Wall Street admitted it has no clear forecast for oil prices amid shifting diplomatic developments and the Trump administration's examination of a possible diesel export ban—a policy that could directly constrain refiner operations and profitability. With refineries running at nearly 97% capacity and multiple geopolitical wildcards in play, investors are pulling back from the refiner trade until the direction becomes clearer.
